paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus shows up for people who are tired, empty-handed and not even sure it's Him. These disciples fished all night and caught nothing, and then a Man on the shore said, "Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some." (John 21:6) They did what He said, and the net was too full to haul in. I've had nights where nothing I did worked, so I'm telling you, the Lord showed up for these men right when their nets were empty. (John 21:3-4)

Notice what He does next: He already has a charcoal fire going with fish on it, and some bread there too, and then He says, "Come, have breakfast." (John 21:9, 12) He still asked them to bring some of their catch (John 21:10), so what they did mattered too. But the breakfast was already waiting, and then Jesus came and gave them the bread and the fish Himself (John 21:13). That's how He treats the ones who follow Him: He asks for your part, and He's still the One who feeds you.

So what do you do with this, baker? Keep showing up, even after a night of nothing, and listen for His voice, because the disciples did not recognize Him at first (John 21:4), and then one of them said, "It is the Lord!" (John 21:7). And when you know it's Him, run to Him like Peter did, with no hesitating. This was now the third time Jesus appeared to His disciples after He was raised from the dead (John 21:14), which tells me He keeps coming back for His people.
